# Quality assurance and audit

> DRAFT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE. Contains claims with status 'ai-extracted' that no clinician has verified.

Unit D13 | Tier: Detect | Version 0.1

## You will be able to

- Name the four things by which the quality of a screening examination is judged.
- Say what should be stored from every cardiac screen, and why.
- Set up a simple audit of your own images and detection.
- Use a checklist for the five planes on every patient.

## What quality means

The quality of a screening examination is judged on four things: image quality, acquisition of the standard planes, appropriate interpretation of the views, and complete documentation. [1]

The 2023 guideline added sections on quality assurance and on the use of a checklist. [2]


## Why it matters

In one retrospective study of missed diagnoses, failure to meet technical criteria contributed to about half of the misses. Failure to recognise abnormal anatomy on an adequate view accounted for nearly a third more. [3]

Both can be measured in your own practice. Stored images show whether the planes met their criteria. Follow-up of outcomes shows whether abnormal hearts were recognised.


## Image quality starts with set-up

Use settings that favour a high frame rate with more contrast and high resolution: low persistence, a single focal zone and a fairly narrow image field. Cardiac presets usually include these. [4]

Magnify until the heart fills at least a third to a half of the screen. [5]


## What to store

Still frames and video clips of the recommended structures and views should be archived, so that the examination can be reviewed later for adequacy. Label laterality and orientation where appropriate. [6]

The upper planes of the sweep are judged more reliably on a clip than on still images. A clip is the better record of them. [7]

For a full fetal echocardiogram, the echocardiography guideline requires both stills and moving clips with a structured report. The clips cover the axial sweep, the four-chamber view, both outflow tracts, the three-vessel views and the sagittal views of both arches. [8]


## Auditing yourself

Audit of stored stills or clips against quality criteria set in advance is encouraged. [9]

Each practice is encouraged to review its own detection rates and diagnostic accuracy every year, and to arrange further training where the review shows a need. [9]

Programmes do better with continuous training based on feedback, standardised protocols, a low threshold for referral and easy access to fetal heart specialists. [10]

One possible routine, for the editor to adjust: once a month, pull a small random set of your own stored cardiac screens. Score each plane against the checklist below as met, not met or not stored. Once a year, list every baby you scanned who was later found to have heart disease, and go back to the stored images of each one.


## The checklist

The checklist below turns the criteria for the five planes into ticks. Use it on every patient until the order is automatic, and use the same list to audit stored studies.

## Five-plane screening checklist

- [ ] Fetal left and right worked out first [11]
- [ ] Upper abdomen: stomach on the left; aorta left of the spine; inferior vena cava right of the spine [12]
- [ ] Heart mainly in the left chest; no larger than a third of the chest area [13, 14]
- [ ] Axis about 45 degrees to the left (plus or minus 20) [14]
- [ ] Rate 120 to 160 per minute, regular [15]
- [ ] Atria similar in size; foramen ovale flap in the left atrium; septum primum present [16]
- [ ] Ventricles similar in size; walls not thick; moderator band in the right ventricle [17, 18]
- [ ] Ventricular septum intact from apex to crux [19]
- [ ] Two atrioventricular valves opening freely; tricuspid inserted nearer the apex [20]
- [ ] LVOT: vessel from the left ventricle, anterior wall continuous with the septum; valve thin, opening freely [21, 22]
- [ ] RVOT: vessel from the right ventricle, dividing after a short course; valve thin, opening freely [23]
- [ ] Great arteries cross and are about equal in size [24, 25]
- [ ] Three-vessel view: three vessels, correct order, size falling from left to right [26]
- [ ] Three-vessel-and-trachea view: V shape, both arches left of the trachea, arches similar in size [27, 28]
- [ ] Stills and clips of each view stored, with laterality labelled [6]

## Still to be written (awaiting sourced claims)

- A scoring system for image quality of each cardiac plane (published criteria with points) - needs a source.
- A target or benchmark detection rate to audit against - needs a source; none is stated in the guideline claims held.
- How long images must be kept and how PC-PNDT record-keeping applies to stored clips in India - needs an Indian legal source and the advisor's input.
- How to obtain outcome feedback after delivery in Indian practice - needs the editor's input.
